records.english: {SPEAKER:A6}Did you notice that lovely scent they were wearing?
records.localization_note: She wonders if her companion noticed how lovely the fragrance was. The question leaves the wearer’s identity to the exchange.
She is pleased that her companion noticed it too. Keep the shared recognition.
She wonders what the fragrance was. Keep the direct question.

records.english: {SPEAKER:A7}I don't know, but it'll catch on.
records.localization_note: She does not know the fragrance but is sure it will catch on. Use a complete sentence that flows into the prediction.

records.english: {SPEAKER:A6}Oh dear! We must obtain it before everyone else.
records.localization_note: She is alarmed at the prospect and wants to obtain it first. Keep her elegant urgency and competitive impulse.
She agrees with the urgency. Keep the brief, polite assent.

records.english: {SPEAKER:A6}Shall we boldly ask them the next time we meet?
records.localization_note: She suggests being bold enough to ask the wearer when they next meet. Keep both the hesitation and timing.

records.english: {SPEAKER:A7}A splendid idea. Let us do exactly that.
records.localization_note: She approves the plan and agrees to do it. Keep the cheerful two-beat answer.
She takes her leave politely. Keep a distinct farewell from her companion’s reply.
She returns the farewell. Keep the succinct response.

records.english: {SYSTEM}Fragrances may soon be all the rage in Lisbon.
records.localization_note: The notice forecasts a trend for scents in Lisbon. Keep the established name for the trade good.

finished_recruitment_before_trend.detail: Yifa asks Li Clan to take her aboard

records.english: {SPEAKER:A6}Oh, that was delicious... I've never had a meal like it.
records.localization_note: She savors the delicious meal and says it is unlike any she has had. Keep her delighted pause and sense of discovery.
She agrees and says the flavors had a stimulating edge. “Had a kick” points naturally toward the chili without claiming she knows the ingredient.

records.english: {SPEAKER:A6}How do you get it to taste so good?
records.localization_note: She asks how such delicious food is made. Keep the practical question and put it on one line.
She chuckles and reveals she has a secret. Keep the playful lead-in to the ingredient.
She gives a puzzled reaction before the ingredient is named. Keep the original brief punctuation beat.

records.english: {SPEAKER:A8}They're called chili peppers, a kind of spice, I'm told. They go beautifully with local ingredients.
records.localization_note: She names chili peppers, says she has heard they are a spice, and finds they suit local ingredients. Keep the reported classification and the local flavor pairing together.
She asks whether the peppers are expensive. Keep her polite concern about the price.
She says they are not especially expensive. Keep the light qualification.

records.english: {SPEAKER:A6}Oh, that's a relief. I may use some for dinner tonight.
records.localization_note: She is relieved and considers using the peppers for dinner that evening. Keep the tentative response, ingredient reference and timing together.
She wants to make it as well. Keep the brief echo of the other woman’s interest.

records.english: {SPEAKER:A8}Then shall I show you how right now?
records.localization_note: She offers to teach them immediately. Keep the hospitable offer and timing.
She reacts with delighted surprise. Keep the short exclamation.
She says the offer is kind. Keep the brief thanks implicit in the compliment.
She says it is only natural because they are friends. Keep the explicitly stated friendship and gracious answer.

records.english: {SYSTEM}Chili peppers may soon be popular in Seoul.
records.localization_note: The notice forecasts a trend for chili peppers in Seoul. Keep the ingredient and the city.
